runbooks.diagnosis: Synapse (1.162.0) removed the legacy API prefixes — /r0/... requests are rejected and /r3/... does not exist at all; only /_matrix/client/v3/ answers. Scripts and bots written against older Matrix client APIs (booking-notify, ai-room-bot, broadcast logic) silently fail with 404.
remediation: Point all client calls at /_matrix/client/v3/... endpoints
Keep the v3 alias resolution and txnId-idempotent sends (retry-safe)
Update any hardcoded /r0/ or /r3/ URLs in scripts that message rooms

runbooks.diagnosis: Synapse SSO used the default localpart_template 'u_<sub>', binding the Zitadel SSO identity to a second u_* account instead of the provisioned @user — and allow_existing_users was unset so the mapping could not bind to the existing account. Missing sso.client_whitelist also forced users through a security 'confirm redirect' interstitial.
remediation: In synapse-setup.sh: map Zitadel preferred_username via localpart_template with u_<sub> fallback
Set allow_existing_users: true so SSO binds the provisioned account
Set sso.client_whitelist to the Element host
Migrate: pre-bind all demo users to their provisioned mxids and deactivate the orphan u_* accounts

runbooks.diagnosis: Three recurring Matrix client pitfalls: (1) the register endpoint needs a MAC computed over the exact (hashed) password bytes sent; (2) docker exec needs -i to deliver a python heredoc on stdin for the MAC script; (3) building curl args via $(...) word-splits an 'Authorization: Bearer <PAT>' header into separate argv words, corrupting the request. 429 responses carry retry_after_ms but naive clients ignore it.
remediation: Compute the register MAC over the exact byte string you send
Use docker exec -i when piping a heredoc into the container
Build curl args in a bash array, never $(...)-word-split auth headers
Honor retry_after_ms from 429s with backoff before retrying
